description: Routing targets for cheque bounce (NI Act §138) cases. Magistrate courts for §138 complaints; DLSA for legal aid.

national.authority_name: Magistrate Court (jurisdiction based on bank branch location)
what_to_bring: Bank return memo / cheque return slip
Copy of demand notice sent under §138
Postal receipt / courier receipt of notice delivery
Copy of the underlying transaction (invoice, agreement, etc.)
Bank statement showing cheque deposit and return
national.filing_fee: Court fees vary by state, typically ₹200-500 for §138 complaint
national.deadline_note: Complaint must be filed within 30 days of expiry of the 15-day notice period (total ~45 days from notice). Court can condone delay up to an additional 30 days for sufficient cause.

maharashtra.authority_name: Metropolitan Magistrate / Judicial Magistrate First Class
what_to_bring: Copy of §138 demand notice with postal proof
maharashtra.filing_fee: ₹200 court fee stamp for §138 complaint in Maharashtra

what_to_bring: Copy of §138 demand notice with postal proof
uttar_pradesh.filing_fee: ₹200 court fee for §138 complaint in UP

karnataka.authority_name: Metropolitan Magistrate / Judicial Magistrate First Class
what_to_bring: Copy of §138 demand notice with postal proof
karnataka.filing_fee: ₹500 court fee for §138 complaint in Karnataka

what_to_bring: Income certificate (if applying for free legal aid)
All documents related to the cheque bounce case
national.deadline_note: Free legal aid available for persons with annual income below ₹3 lakh (varies by state). No deadline to apply.

what_to_bring: Any correspondence with the other party
All documents related to the case
